decisions.statement: A rule is handed one file already parsed.
A rule is handed what the pages declare, since a rule reads no index of its own.
A rule is handed what each level of the command tree names itself.
A rule is handed whether a level is a command or a namespace.
A rule asks what one module declares rather than holding every module's answer.
A call is found in the parse and never in the text.
A rule is handed every file its own mark does not excuse.
Every rule whose mark the file carries judges that file.
A rule stating no mark is handed every file.
A mark excuses a file only where that rule could not have refused it.
A rule states its mark in the file that holds the pattern the mark is taken from.
No table of marks is kept, since a mark apart from its pattern would stale unseen.
A rule names the line the rule refuses.
A rule refusing nothing found nothing.
A rule not ready to judge is not written.

definition: a pattern a source file may not carry
